text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — node 'gpu-prod-12' reporting ephemeral storage saturation and multiple serve-runtime restarts (pod evictions). Alert group: oncall-inference. https://alerts.example/alert/2150004321

incident-bot: Summary: /scratch usage 98%, rapid inode exhaustion on /var/lib/model-cache, 3x pod restarts in last 2m, some containers showing CUDA OOMs in logs.

sara: grabbing it — oncall. I'm seeing the same in console. Starting with node check.

devon: paste: ``kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-prod-12`` shows ~6 modelcache pods, 4 in CrashLoopBackOff, 2 Running.

devon: paste: ``kubectl describe pod modelcache-xyz`` -> Events: "Back-off restarting failed container", "Evicted: The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage"

devon: quick df: ``ssh gpu-prod-12 df -h /scratch`` -> `/scratch  1.8T 1.8T  1G  99%`

sara: logs show repeated modelcache writes + large rotation of debug logs. Something wrote huge logs + cache shards.

mike: @sara @devon I'm joining. First thought: modelcache growth + log writeback causing tmpfs/scratch fill and kernel eviction of pods. GPU tasks hitting CUDA OOM when restarted due to partial KV cache.

ash: pinging infra to see if there's a runaway cron or backup job writing to /scratch.

devon: found log pattern: modelcache shard flush loop: ``shard_writer: flushed 45GiB in 12s`` repeated. Also see ``CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`` after restart in serve runtime logs.

sara: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon node, 2) scale down modelcache replicas on that node (evict noncritical), 3) free space: remove rotated logs + temp shards, 4) route traffic to fallback region/model.

mike: doing cordon: ``kubectl cordon gpu-prod-12`` -> success.

mike: starting forced delete of non-ready modelcache pods to drop write pressure: ``kubectl delete pod modelcache-xyz --grace-period=0 --force`` (doing this one by one).

devon: I'm removing largest logs under /scratch/logs/modelcache/* older than 2d: ``ssh gpu-prod-12 'find /scratch/logs/modelcache -type f -mtime +2 -delete'`` — reclaimed ~320GiB so far.

ash: I found a recent rollout that accidentally enabled --debug-io on modelcache. That explains the heavy writes. Reverting flag now.

mike: added temporary eviction rule to prefer nodes with >20% free scratch. Patching node selector on Deployment to avoid gpu-prod-12.

ops-bot: Auto-scaling adjustment: lowered modelcache replicas by 50% cluster-wide to reduce aggregate disk pressure.

sara: rerouting traffic to fallback smaller model for latency-tolerant customers. Updating routing: ``/api/v1/route?model=small-fallback``.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff: sara -> mike accepted at 2150004560.

mike: I'm taking lead. Next: run fsck and check inode usage: ``ssh gpu-prod-12 'df -i /scratch'`` -> inodes 99% used. We need to purge tiny temp files created by a bug.

devon: found many tiny .tmp shard files from a failed merge loop. Running ``find /scratch/modelcache -name '*.tmp' -delete`` recovered ~120k inodes, freed ~18GB.

mike: After deletions, scratch at 65% usage, pods can start. I'm restarting 2 model serve pods slowly to avoid simultaneous CUDA warmup spikes. Command: ``kubectl rollout restart deploy/serve-runtime -n inference --field-selector spec.nodeName!=gpu-prod-12``

sara: customer impact: some requests to heavy models from EU region had 503s for ~7 minutes. I flagged customer support to notify top 5 accounts that hit error rates.

ash: confirm rollback of debug flag completed and new image not pushed; CI avoided the option.

devon: monitoring: disk pressure metric is trending down, pod restarts falling to 0. Observability link: https://console.example/metrics/node/gpu-prod-12

mike: running targeted health checks on restarted pods, checking KV cache integrity. No corruption seen in latest quick checks.

sara: quick customer note draft: "We experienced a spike in ephemeral storage usage on node gpu-prod-12 that caused pod evictions and transient 5xx errors. We mitigated by cordoning the node, removing temporary files, disabling a debug write flag, and shifting traffic to fallback models. Service has recovered; follow-up postmortem will include RCA and preventive actions." Agree to send? :thumbsup:

mike: :thumbsup: go ahead. I'll add technical appendix in postmortem.

ops-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-7894 and linked to oncall timeline.

sara: follow-ups: 1) expedite a patch to prevent temp-file explosion (PR#4523), 2) add alert for inode pressure (not just disk usage), 3) limit debug-io flag via feature gate.

devon: scheduling a controlled node drain to run full fs cleanup and kernel tuning in maintenance window.

mike: final check: node uncordon after cleanup? I'm keeping it cordoned until maintenance.

sara: last checks show 200s p95 latency normalizing. I'll mark incident as mitigated and hand off to postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated by actions from sara, mike, devon, ash. Please fill postmortem template: https://confluence.example/incidents/INC-2026-7894

sara: closing thread, moving to postmortem. Thanks all for quick ops. :heart:
